proposals.stance: Agents earn autonomy by running under review first; autonomy is not a setting you switch on.
proposals.why_we_believe_it: Our platform sends every agent change through review before production, and our approvals post argues that trust comes from a record of reviewed runs. We have seen teams widen an agent's scope only after that record exists.

evidence.quote: Autonomy is something an agent earns after it has run under review, not a setting you switch on.
Every agent change goes through review before it reaches production.

proposals.applies_when: A vendor or large company announces fully autonomous agents, agent guardrails or an agent governance framework.
proposals.counter_position: Ship autonomy now and add guardrails as problems appear. We concede it for throwaway internal prototypes with no customer data.
proposals.never_say: That agents should never act without a person: we argue for earned autonomy, not permanent approval.

proposals.stance: Most agent demos never reach production; the real test is whether it still works on day thirty.
proposals.why_we_believe_it: Our post on why demos die and the founders' customer calls both describe agents that impress once and are dropped within a week. We build for the day-thirty run, not the demo.

evidence.quote: A demo that works once is not an agent; an agent is the thing that still works on day thirty.
most agent demos never survive their first week in a real team.

proposals.applies_when: A company shows an impressive agent demo, launch video or benchmark result without production use.
proposals.counter_position: Demos are how new categories start and buyers learn what is possible. True, but a demo is a promise, not a product.
proposals.never_say: A failure rate or number we have not measured.

questions.question: Our writing does not say how agents should be priced: per run, per seat or per outcome. Which do we believe?

> "Autonomy is something an agent earns after it has run under review, not a setting you switch on." <https://acme.example.com/blog/approvals-before-autonomy|Approvals before autonomy>
> "Every agent change goes through review before it reaches production." <https://acme.example.com/platform|Platform>

*Use it when*
A vendor or large company announces fully autonomous agents, agent guardrails or an agent governance framework.

*The other side*
Ship autonomy now and add guardrails as problems appear. We concede it for throwaway internal prototypes with no customer data.

*Why we believe it*
Our post on why demos die and the founders' customer calls both describe agents that impress once and are dropped within a week. We build for the day-thirty run, not the demo.

*Evidence*
> "A demo that works once is not an agent; an agent is the thing that still works on day thirty." <https://acme.example.com/blog/why-demos-die|Why demos die>
> "most agent demos never survive their first week in a real team." — founder notes

*Use it when*
A company shows an impressive agent demo, launch video or benchmark result without production use.

*The other side*
Demos are how new categories start and buyers learn what is possible. True, but a demo is a promise, not a product.
